records.summary: Certain areas emit dangerous levels of radiation. Entering these zones requires Constitution saving throws (DC 14) every 10 minutes. Failure results in 1 level of exhaustion from radiation sickness and potential long-term effects without medical treatment.

Security scanners and drones monitor for contraband, weapons, or unauthorized personnel. When near a scanner or drone, characters with hidden items must make Dexterity (Stealth) checks (DC 14) or trigger an alarm, summoning security personnel.

Nebula gases interfere with sensors and communications. Any attempt to use navigational tools, scanners, or communicators requires an Intelligence (Technology) check (DC 15). Failure results in malfunctions or complete signal loss for 1d4 hours.

Time behaves erratically in the convergence, with some areas looping or slowing down. Roll a d20 every hour; on a 1-5, a time loop occurs, causing characters to repeat actions unknowingly or lose track of time. Wisdom (Insight) checks (DC 14) may reveal the loop.

•High-Speed Winds: Constantly shifting winds reach speeds up to 200 mph, requiring Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) every 10 minutes for ships and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks for individuals to avoid being buffeted or swept off course. •Electrical Storms: Thunderstorms with massive lightning strikes are common. Unshielded characters or ships must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to avoid 2d6 lightning damage from sudden strikes. •Crushing Pressure at Lower Depths: Descending further into the atmosphere increases pressure dramatically. Characters without specialized suits or reinforced vessels risk Constitution saving throws (DC 15) to avoid exhaustion or damage.

Lower levels suffer from pollution and contaminated air due to industrial activity. Characters in these areas must make Constitution saving throws (DC 13) every 2 hours to avoid mild poisoning, which imposes disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks until they leave the area.

•Ship pilots must make Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 15) every 10 minutes to navigate around floating debris and unstable wrecks. A failed check results in minor collisions, dealing 2d6 damage to the shipʼs hull or shields. •Tethering to stable wreckage or using propulsion devices grants advantage on maneuvering checks in areas with dense debris.

•Characters or ships encountering a temporal flare must make Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 15) to adjust their timepieces and avoid time slippage. Failure may cause them to exit the wormhole hours or even days after they entered.

•Characters within time dilation fields may lose track of time without realizing it. Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 14) are required every hour to maintain awareness of time. Failure may result in losing hours or even days, depending on proximity.
•Many doors are jammed or require manual overrides. Bypassing them requires Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 14) or Strength checks (DC 15) to force them open. Some doors may

•Propulsion devices allow for controlled movement but require Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 13) to change direction or navigate around fast-moving objects. A failed check may result in a drift, causing disorientation and potential collision.

Bustling areas like markets and entertainment zones are rife with pickpockets and hustlers. Characters without secured items may fall victim to thieves; make a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 13) to notice the attempt, or lose a random small item.

Open space alternates between extreme cold and intense sunlight. Characters without thermal shielding experience temperature fluctuations that require Constitution saving throws (DC 13) every 10 minutes to avoid 1d6 cold or radiant damage. 4.Oxygen Supply Limitations: Space suits have limited oxygen supplies, usually enough for 8 hours. For each hour without a refill, characters must track their oxygen use carefully. Once oxygen is depleted, characters begin to suffocate.
Prolonged isolation and darkness create an unsettling atmosphere. Characters may hear strange sounds or see apparitions, requiring Wisdom saving throws (DC 13) to resist paranoia or hallucinations.

Ghostly echoes of lost transmissions play through the nebula, confusing navigators. Attempting to decode these signals requires Intelligence (Investigation) checks (DC 14) to separate real communications from ghostly echoes, potentially leading to lost relics or expeditions.

Some asteroids exert weak gravitational pulls, pulling nearby objects or individuals off-course. Characters passing through these fields must make Strength checks (DC 13) to resist the pull or risk drifting toward the asteroid.

Gravity pockets can pull characters or ships suddenly downward. Entering a pocket requires Strength checks (DC 15) to resist, or characters are dragged toward lower atmospheric layers, suffering 2d6 crushing damage for every failed save as the pressure increases. 4.Poisonous Gas Clouds: Certain gas giant atmospheres contain poisonous gases. Passing through these clouds requires Constitution saving throws (DC 14) every 10 minutes to avoid poisoning (disadvantage on Dexterity checks and saving throws for 1 hour).

Strange creatures, such as space-adapted vermin, thrive within the debris. They may be territorial or predatory, ambushing characters who venture too close. Players may need to make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to avoid surprise attacks.

Some wrecks have dormant or malfunctioning weapon systems that can reactivate. Characters coming close must succeed on Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid 3d6 fire or energy damage from sudden attacks. Tripping hidden mines or grenades inside the wrecks can deal 2d6 piercing or explosive damage.
Old security systems on derelict ships or stations may still be active, firing on anything nearby. Characters must succeed on Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid laser fire or EMP blasts.

•Maintenance shafts and hidden corridors provide shortcuts but are narrow and dangerous. Moving through these requires Dexterity (Stealth) checks (DC 13) to avoid detection, and characters may encounter power surges or ventilation malfunctions.

The proximity of wormholes creates sensor interference and navigation glitches. Ships or characters using technology to navigate must make Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 15) to recalibrate systems. Failure may cause sudden detours or inaccurate coordinates.

•Entering restricted areas, such as upper districts or faction strongholds, requires passing security checkpoints. Characters must succeed on Charisma (Deception) or Dexterity (Stealth) checks (DC 15) to avoid drawing security attention.

Characters near the black hole encounter spatial distortions, areas where space behaves unpredictably. Characters moving through these regions must succeed on Intelligence saving throws (DC 15) to avoid disorientation or find themselves inexplicably teleported a short distance.

Shifting lights and colors can cause disorientation. Characters must make Wisdom saving throws (DC 14) every hour to avoid becoming lost, veering off course, or misinterpreting distances due to illusions.

Due to constant atmospheric stress, floating stations frequently need repairs. Characters may encounter damaged outposts requiring manual adjustments or repair checks (Intelligence, DC 13) to stabilize.

•Electrical storms disrupt sensor systems, causing disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sensors. Manual navigation with Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 14) is required to avoid these disruptions. •Ships equipped with atmospheric stabilization gear have advantage on navigation checks to avoid storms but must still roll against high winds.

Time-warped phenomena can create “phantoms” or mirages of past events. Characters encountering these echoes must make Wisdom saving throws (DC 15) to avoid becoming disoriented or drawn into repeating loops of the events they witness.

Damaged labs or industrial areas may release toxic chemicals. Characters passing through must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 14) or become poisoned for 1 hour. Extended exposure (more than 10 minutes) may result in levels of exhaustion.

Terminals may contain logs revealing the stationʼs fate or warnings of dangers. Accessing these terminals requires Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 13) and may be interrupted by system glitches or attract hostile creatures.

Small, fast-moving particles occasionally move through the field. Roll a d12 every 30 minutes. On a 1, a micrometeor shower strikes, requiring Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid 1d6 piercing damage from micrometeor impacts.

Small energy storms or plasma arcs occasionally surge through the nebula. Characters or ships passing through them must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid 2d6 lightning damage from sudden energy discharges.

Competing factions occasionally clash, turning sections of the city into war zones. Characters must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid stray gunfire, explosions, or being swept into protests and riots.

Intense magnetic activity interferes with communication and sensors. Characters must rely on Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 14) to spot hazards without technological assistance, potentially becoming lost or caught in high winds.

Convergence zones sometimes create “phantom” wormholes—visual illusions that appear as real entry points. Characters attempting to enter these areas must make Wisdom saving throws (DC 13) to avoid disorientation or risk ending up back where they started.

With travelers from countless worlds, infections spread quickly. Every 24 hours, roll a d20. On a 1, an area goes into temporary quarantine, restricting access and potentially exposing characters to a disease requiring a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) to avoid contracting symptoms.

Some wrecks contain high-value resources in locked or encrypted storage. Accessing these may require Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 15) to bypass security or Strength checks (DC 14) to force access. Opening containers may also reveal traps or summon scavenger rivals. 5.Malfunctioning Defense Drones: Some wrecks have defense drones that, while nonfunctional for years, may still activate upon detecting intruders. These drones attack anyone nearby unless disabled with Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 15).

Rich deposits of plasma crystals, ionized gases, or rare elements may be found but often lie within high-radiation or energy-anomalous areas. Characters scavenging in these zones must make Constitution saving throws (DC 15) every 10 minutes to avoid exhaustion or radiation poisoning.

When resources are scarce, characters can scavenge or barter for essential supplies. Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks (DC 13) may reveal useful items, but scavenging can attract gangs or security patrols.

Sudden power outages, gravity fluctuations, or air leaks can occur in high-traffic areas. Characters may need to make Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid falling, colliding, or suffering minor injuries when systems fail.
